features.description: Single generated operating brief. Add an agent_brief module that renders DontPanic's operator guide from live source-of-truth data: agent_manifest supported commands, dontpanic version, AGENT_REGISTRY executor names, config-home status, and canonical workflow commands. The brief explicitly distinguishes interactive operators from dispatchable worker executors and states that DontPanic local orchestration is not Kubernetes, Airflow, or generic IT orchestration.
steps: Add scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/agent_brief.py with typed brief input/output helpers and deterministic text rendering.
Use agent_manifest supported command generation instead of duplicating command lists by hand.
Use executors.AGENT_REGISTRY for worker executor names.
Include the operator-vs-worker paragraph and the not-Kubernetes/Airflow clarification.
Include canonical workflow: projects add, plan lock, orchestrate/dispatch-from-plan, approve/resume/close.
Expose a content hash and generator version for managed repo blocks.
Add tests proving command and executor changes affect the generated brief without hand-editing strings in multiple places.
features.acceptance: (1) agent_brief renders deterministic text from live manifest and executor registry data. (2) Brief contains the operator-vs-worker distinction. (3) Brief warns that DontPanic orchestration is local CLI workflow orchestration, not Kubernetes/Airflow/IT orchestration. (4) Brief lists current supported commands from agent_manifest, including agent and orchestrate after F002. (5) Brief lists current worker executors from AGENT_REGISTRY and does not include unsupported labels. (6) Brief exposes generator version and content hash. (7) Tests mutate fake command/executor inputs and prove the rendered brief updates from source data.

features.description: Machine agent surface and orchestrate gateway. Add `dontpanic agent brief`, `dontpanic agent status`, `dontpanic agent setup <name>`, a guarded `dontpanic agent register-worker <name>` path for implemented executors only, plus `dontpanic orchestrate`. The agent surface prints the generated brief for newly installed interactive agents, classifies whether the current agent is operator-only or worker-capable, and makes it obvious when no worker registration is possible because no executor exists. The orchestrate command is a teaching gateway: no args or invalid args print the brief plus workflow; a plan id/path forwards to dispatch-from-plan while preserving existing dry-run behavior unless --confirm is supplied. Update the manifest supported_commands accordingly.
steps: Add top-level `agent` subcommand with `brief`, `status`, `setup <name>`, and guarded `register-worker <name>` help text.
Wire `dontpanic agent brief` to agent_brief renderer.
Wire `dontpanic agent status` to print installed/known operator agents, registered worker executors, configured roles, and whether the named/current agent can be dispatched.
Wire `dontpanic agent setup <name>` to produce operator setup guidance for any named interactive agent and worker setup guidance only when the executor is implemented.
Implement `dontpanic agent register-worker <name>` as a guarded path that refuses unknown executors with a clear message and only writes config when `<name>` resolves to AGENT_REGISTRY.
Add top-level `orchestrate` command.
For `dontpanic orchestrate` with no args, --help, or invalid shape, print the generated brief and canonical workflow.
For `dontpanic orchestrate <plan-id-or-path> [dispatch flags]`, forward to _dispatch_from_plan_main with equivalent argv.
Preserve dispatch-from-plan dry-run-by-default behavior.
Update agent_manifest supported_commands with agent and orchestrate.
Add CLI tests for help, no-arg teaching output, forwarding behavior, manifest content, and invalid input.
features.acceptance: (1) `dontpanic agent brief` prints the generated brief and exits 0. (2) `dontpanic agent status` classifies current/named agents as operator-only or worker-capable from AGENT_REGISTRY and role config. (3) `dontpanic agent setup grok` explains that Grok can operate DontPanic but cannot be registered as a worker without an executor. (4) `dontpanic agent register-worker <unknown>` refuses without writing config; `register-worker claude/codex` writes only valid role config according to the selected flags. (5) `dontpanic orchestrate` with no args prints the brief/workflow and exits 0 or 2 with actionable text, per existing CLI convention selected in implementation. (6) `dontpanic orchestrate <plan>` forwards to dispatch-from-plan without changing dry-run semantics. (7) `dontpanic orchestrate <plan> --confirm` reaches the same path as `dispatch-from-plan <plan> --confirm`. (8) `dontpanic manifest show/init` includes agent and orchestrate in supported_commands. (9) Tests cover the gateway and do not invoke real agent CLIs.

features.description: Repo onboarding managed block. Add `projects add --onboard` and a reusable managed-block writer. Onboarding creates or updates `.dontpanic/dontpanic.json` with explicit defaults, inserts a marked generated DontPanic block into AGENTS.md, and creates or updates a CLAUDE.md pointer block. Existing repo instructions outside markers are never touched. Dry-run previews all writes. Re-running onboarding updates stale managed blocks based on generator version/hash.
steps: Add an onboarding writer module with create/update/remove-free managed block helpers.
Define stable markers containing generator version and content hash.
Add `projects add --onboard` and `--dry-run` flags.
When onboarded, write `.dontpanic/dontpanic.json` with explicit known fields rather than bare `{}`.
Create AGENTS.md when missing; otherwise insert or replace only the managed DontPanic block.
Create CLAUDE.md when missing as a short pointer to AGENTS.md; otherwise insert or replace only the managed pointer block.
Preserve lowercase `.claude.md` without assuming agents will read it; optionally warn when only lowercase exists.
Add tests for missing files, existing files, stale block update, fresh block no-op, dry-run, JSON output, and no writes outside markers.
features.acceptance: (1) `dontpanic projects add NAME PATH --onboard --dry-run` reports all intended writes without changing files. (2) `--onboard` creates `.dontpanic/dontpanic.json` with explicit defaults and a schema-compatible shape. (3) Missing AGENTS.md is created with the generated brief block. (4) Existing AGENTS.md content outside markers remains byte-for-byte unchanged. (5) Stale managed block is updated in place when hash/version differ. (6) Fresh managed block is left unchanged. (7) CLAUDE.md is created or updated as a pointer/alias without clobbering existing content. (8) Tests cover JSON and human output.

features.description: Simple worker role assignment. Add CLI and dashboard-friendly role assignment surfaces for `roles.implementer`, `roles.auditor`, and `roles.goal_auditor`. The surface lists available worker executors from AGENT_REGISTRY, shows effective current roles with source layer (project roles, project legacy, global roles, global legacy, fallback), supports global and per-project writes, previews changes, and refuses unsupported operator-only agents. This is the low-friction path for requests like 'use Codex as auditor for this project' without hand-editing JSON.
steps: Add a role assignment helper that resolves current role values and source layer for implementer, auditor, and goal_auditor.

Add CLI surface such as `dontpanic roles show [--project NAME|PATH]` and `dontpanic roles set <role> <executor> [--project NAME|PATH|--global] [--dry-run] [--yes]`, or an equivalent shape consistent with existing config commands.
List available worker executors from AGENT_REGISTRY in role show/help output.
Refuse role assignment to names not present in AGENT_REGISTRY, with wording that operator-only agents can operate DontPanic but cannot be assigned as workers.
Make scope explicit: global write updates ~/.dontpanic/config.json roles.*, project write updates <repo>/.dontpanic/dontpanic.json roles.*.
Expose a dashboard state projection shape for role assignment: available executors, current effective roles, source layer, project/global scope, and safe mutation command.
Add dashboard action/mutation contract tests or state-shape tests without requiring a browser mutation backend.
Add tests for global role set, project role set, dry-run, unknown executor refusal, source-layer display, goal_auditor fallback, and dashboard projection shape.
features.acceptance: (1) A human or interactive agent can list available worker executors and current effective role assignments without reading JSON. (2) Assigning `auditor codex --project myrepo` writes the project roles block and leaves global config untouched. (3) Assigning `implementer claude --global` writes the global roles block. (4) Dry-run previews the exact file and value change. (5) Unknown executor names such as Grok-Builder are refused before writes. (6) Output explains operator-only versus worker-capable when refusal happens. (7) Dashboard state includes enough structured data to render role pickers and safe mutation commands. (8) Tests cover role resolution source layers and mutation targets.

features.description: Doctor validation for machine and project onboarding. Add `doctor --agent` and `doctor --project <name-or-path>` checks backed by the same generated brief data. Validate CLI/manifest availability, executor registry, role resolution for both legacy implementer/auditor and roles.* fields, managed-block freshness, and repo onboarding status. `roles.implementer=Grok-Builder` or any other non-registered executor must fail clearly.
steps: Add agent-level doctor checks: dontpanic on PATH or module invocable, manifest present/current, generated brief renders, executor registry non-empty, command list includes agent/orchestrate.

Add project-level doctor checks: project registered or path-resolved, `.dontpanic/dontpanic.json` valid, AGENTS.md managed block present/current, CLAUDE.md pointer present/current or intentionally skipped.
Extend existing project agent validation to include project `roles.*` and global `roles.*`, not just legacy implementer/auditor fields.
Report resolved role chain with source layer: per-call, project roles, project legacy, global roles, global legacy, fallback.
Expose executor list in doctor output so an interactive agent can classify itself as operator-only or worker-capable.
Keep existing `doctor --include-projects` compatible by reusing the new project validation helpers.
Add tests for unknown global roles, unknown project roles, stale managed block, missing block, current block, and operator-only agent interpretation.
features.acceptance: (1) `dontpanic doctor --agent` validates the machine onboarding layer and prints registered worker executors. (2) `dontpanic doctor --project NAME` validates one project and its managed onboarding block. (3) Unknown global `roles.*` values fail. (4) Unknown project `roles.*` values fail. (5) Legacy implementer/auditor validation still works. (6) Stale or missing managed repo block is reported with an exact `projects add --onboard` remediation. (7) Existing doctor tests remain compatible. (8) Tests prove `Grok-Builder` is flagged as unrunnable unless registered in AGENT_REGISTRY.

features.description: Config-home reconciliation. Replace silent ~/.dontpanic versus ~/.jarvis split-brain behavior with an explicit reconcile path. Doctor detects contradictory homes; a reconcile command previews differences, migrates missing canonical files into ~/.dontpanic, preserves legacy ~/.jarvis as read-through compatibility, and refuses ambiguous destructive merges without --confirm.
steps: Inventory all files read or written under DontPanic and legacy Jarvis homes, including config.json, projects.json, agent-manifest.json, dashboard state, quota files, and adapters.
Add config-home comparison helpers that classify identical, missing-in-canonical, missing-in-legacy, divergent, and unsupported shapes.
Add a CLI surface such as `dontpanic reconcile homes --dry-run` and `--confirm` or extend existing reconcile with a home-state subcommand.
Migrate agent-manifest.json into ~/.dontpanic when only legacy exists.
Migrate non-conflicting missing canonical files from ~/.jarvis to ~/.dontpanic with backups where needed.
Refuse divergent same-name files without an explicit operator choice; never silently pick one.
Update doctor --agent to fail or warn according to severity and point to the reconcile command.
Add tests using isolated home dirs for identical homes, legacy-only manifest, divergent role configs, divergent project registries, migration success, and ambiguity refusal.
features.acceptance: (1) Doctor surfaces split-brain ~/.dontpanic vs ~/.jarvis state with file-level details. (2) Reconcile dry-run prints an exact migration plan and writes nothing. (3) Reconcile confirm migrates non-conflicting legacy-only files into ~/.dontpanic. (4) agent-manifest.json ends up in the canonical home after reconcile. (5) Divergent config.json and projects.json are not silently merged. (6) Legacy read-through compatibility remains for old installs after migration. (7) Tests cover all classification states and write behavior in isolated homes.

features.description: Budget, quota, cooldown, iteration, gate-finalization, and setup decision guidance. Add a small decision engine and CLI/dashboard surfaces that convert common operational blockers into a short set of recommended choices with exact commands and tradeoffs. Cases include quota cooldown, budget ceiling exceeded, admission threshold mismatch, max_iterations remaining/exhausted, signed_off volley paused at pre_merge, no-progress stop, missing project registration, stale repo onboarding, stale agent brief, unsupported worker role, split config homes, and human-required configuration. The goal is that a human or interactive agent should not spend multiple reasoning cycles deciding whether to wait, redispatch, raise a ceiling, finalize a cleared pre_merge signoff, resume, close, onboard, reconcile, open the dashboard, or answer a human-required setup question.
steps: Add an operations guidance module that consumes existing quota/admission/iteration/gate/project/doctor state and emits typed ActionChoice records: recommended action, alternatives, exact_command where safe, rationale, risk, and required human confirmation.
Expose a CLI surface such as `dontpanic what-now` or extend `dontpanic next`/`doctor` with an operations-guidance section for blocked current work.
For quota cooldown, calculate and display wait-until time when available, then the exact redispatch command.
For budget ceiling or admission threshold blockers, show both wait/redispatch and raise-ceiling/raise-threshold paths, including the safer recommended default.
For max_iterations state, display remaining fix iterations, whether redispatch would run within cap, and the exact command to continue or close.

For signed_off audits paused at pre_merge, display whether pre_merge is still pending or cleared; when cleared, offer and support a no-paid-call finalization action that writes or repairs the signoff envelope and flips features.json from the existing signed_off audit artifacts.

Add a no-paid finalizer, such as `dontpanic finalize <plan> --feature <F>` or an equivalent command, that gates on the latest auditor artifact being signed_off plus cleared pre_merge state, reuses closeout._flip_feature_passes or a shared helper without entering the operator-resolved/no_progress path, repairs the signoff envelope if the pre_merge pause skipped _emit_volley_terminal, and writes evidence_refs.
For exhausted iterations or no-progress stops, display approve/resume/close choices with the current gate/breaker name and risk text.
For setup friction, recommend `projects add --onboard`, `doctor --agent`, `doctor --project`, `agent brief`, or home reconcile when the state indicates they are needed.

When any ActionChoice requires human input, attach one response-level dashboard affordance: active URL if a dashboard singleton is running, otherwise the exact command to start the dashboard. Individual choices may reference the affordance by id but must not repeat the full dashboard text.
Surface the same ActionChoice records in dashboard what-now/action items so decisions are available without re-reading CLI logs.
Add tests for the concrete example: Codex budget cooling plus remaining max_iterations recommends waiting and redispatching, with an alternative raise-ceiling path.
Add tests for missing project registration, stale onboarding block, unsupported roles.*, budget ceiling exceeded, admission threshold mismatch, iterations exhausted, and no-progress stop.
features.acceptance: (1) A blocked quota/cooldown case renders a recommended wait-until + redispatch action and a separate raise-ceiling/threshold alternative when applicable. (2) The guidance explicitly states remaining max_iterations and whether the next fix iteration is within cap. (3) Budget and iteration guidance appears in CLI output and dashboard ActionItems from the same typed ActionChoice data. (4) A signed_off volley paused at pre_merge shows the gate state; after pre_merge is cleared, guidance offers a no-paid-call finalization action instead of forcing a fresh paid dispatch. (5) Setup guidance tells humans/agents when to run projects add --onboard, doctor --agent, doctor --project, agent brief, or home reconcile. (6) Human-required output includes exactly one response-level dashboard affordance: active URL when running, start command when not running; individual choices do not repeat it. (7) Exact commands are emitted only when safe AND validated against the live CLI grammar. "Validated" means: every emitted exact_command is a runnable invocation with the correct subcommand and all required arguments (it must not exit 2 on a usage error), and it respects current state. Concretely: (7a) no redispatch/orchestrate command is emitted when the next fix iteration would exceed max_iterations (exhausted state offers close/finalize or human action, never a redispatch command); (7b) no bare `dontpanic resume <plan>` — resume commands must carry the required `--gate <name>` or `--all`; (7c) no bare `dontpanic reconcile` — it must name the `homes` subcommand (e.g. `dontpanic reconcile homes --dry-run`); (7d) any response-level dashboard affordance referenced by an ActionItem must actually be present in the rendered dashboard cache, not merely named in detail text; (7e) re-onboarding guidance for an already-registered project emits `projects add <name> <path> --onboard --force --yes` (a bare `--onboard` is invalid because the registry refuses an existing name without --force --yes). When a valid command cannot be formed, guidance says human action required (requires_human) with advisory text instead of emitting a bare or invalid command. (8) Tests cover at least nine decision states, including the Codex cooldown + max_iterations example, signed_off/pre_merge finalization, active/inactive dashboard hints, and dashboard-hint deduplication; tests must also assert each of 7a–7e directly (exhausted-iteration emits no redispatch command; resume carries --gate/--all; reconcile names homes; referenced dashboard affordance is present in the built cache; already-registered re-onboard carries --force --yes). (9) A signed_off-and-pre_merge-cleared feature can be finalized with zero paid agent calls: a `dontpanic finalize <plan> --feature <F>` command, or equivalent, consumes the existing signed_off auditor artifact plus cleared gate-state, writes or repairs `signoff-<plan>.json`, and flips only that feature's passes:true with evidence_refs pointing at the audit artifact. (10) The finalizer refuses without mutation if the latest audit verdict is not signed_off, if pre_merge is uncleared, or if no audit envelope exists, with distinct exit codes per case. (11) The finalizer is idempotent and never triggers `dispatch_volley` or any worker executor invocation. (12) Tests prove clean signed_off to passes:true with no executor invocation, refusal on needs_changes, refusal on uncleared pre_merge, missing-audit refusal, and idempotent re-run. (Scope, per D035 split: F007 covers the decision engine, exact_command validity (7a–7e), and the no-paid finalizer with their CLI + dashboard rendering. Live-path completeness — every setup/doctor guidance state reachable from BOTH `what-now` and the dashboard, and ActionItem IDs carrying feature_id so distinct features do not collapse — is delegated to F012 and is OUT OF SCOPE for F007.)

features.description: Live-path completeness for the F007 operations-guidance surface. F007 built the decision engine and its quota/budget/iteration/finalize states reachable from `what-now` and the dashboard, but the setup/doctor guidance states (missing project registration, stale onboarding, unsupported roles, doctor --agent, doctor --project, agent brief, home reconcile) are computed only in the builder and are not surfaced through the live `collect_state()` path, so they are unreachable from `dontpanic what-now` and the dashboard. Additionally, dashboard ActionItem IDs omit feature_id, so distinct blocked features sharing a choice kind collapse into one item. This slice wires the full setup/doctor surface into the live path with CLI+dashboard parity and makes ActionItem IDs feature-scoped.
steps: Extend `collect_state()` so the live path derives every setup/doctor guidance state F007's builder can emit: missing registration, stale onboarding, unsupported roles.*, doctor --agent, doctor --project, agent brief, and home reconcile.

Ensure `dontpanic what-now [--feature F]` renders each setup/doctor state with its validated exact_command or requires_human advisory (reusing F007's exact_command validity rules, including the --force --yes re-onboard case).
Render the same setup/doctor ActionChoices into dashboard ActionItems so CLI and dashboard reach parity for setup guidance, not just quota/budget/iteration.

Make dashboard ActionItem IDs feature-scoped (include feature_id) so multiple blocked features with the same choice kind do not dedupe into a single item; preserve intentional plan-level blocker dedup.
Add tests proving each setup/doctor state is reachable from BOTH what-now and the built dashboard cache, and that two features with the same choice kind produce two distinct ActionItems.
features.acceptance: (1) `collect_state()` (the live path used by `dontpanic what-now` and the dashboard) derives every setup/doctor guidance state F007's builder emits: missing registration, stale onboarding, unsupported roles.*, doctor --agent, doctor --project, agent brief, and home reconcile — none are builder-only/unreachable. (2) `dontpanic what-now` renders each of those setup/doctor states with a validated exact_command (per F007 7a–7e) or a requires_human advisory when no safe command exists. (3) The dashboard renders the same setup/doctor ActionChoices as ActionItems, achieving CLI+dashboard parity for setup guidance. (4) Dashboard ActionItem IDs include feature_id so two distinct blocked features sharing a choice kind produce two distinct items; intentional plan-level blocker dedup is preserved. (5) Tests prove each setup/doctor state is reachable from BOTH what-now and the built dashboard cache, and that two same-kind blocked features yield two distinct ActionItems (no collapse). (6) "Validated exact_command" means the command actually PASSES `command_validation.validate_command_tokens` (not merely that a string matches): `command_validation.py` must recognize every command operations_guidance can emit across all states — including `agent brief`, `finalize <plan> --feature <F>`, `what-now <plan> --feature <F>`, `orchestrate <plan>`, `doctor --agent`, `doctor --project <name>`, `reconcile homes [--dry-run]`, and `projects add <name> <path> --onboard --force --yes`. Any state whose command does NOT pass the validator must emit `requires_human` advisory with `exact_command=None` instead of an invalid string. (7) A test iterates EVERY non-null `exact_command` emitted by `build_guidance`/`collect_state` across all quota/budget/iteration/finalize/setup/doctor states and asserts each passes `validate_command_tokens` (stripping the `dontpanic`/`python -m dontpanic_orchestrate` prefix) — this is what makes the green suite actually prove validity (closing the codex i2 gap where string-equality tests let invalid shapes through).

features.description: Configuration inventory and setup cockpit. Add a unified config inventory that lets humans and interactive agents assess, configure, and update every core DontPanic surface without spelunking files or prompting through long reasoning loops. Inventory entries include global config, per-project config, role assignments, project registry, agent manifest, capability manifests, adapters, runtime evidence defaults, human gates/protected paths/plans_dir, quota state/caps/calibration/admission thresholds, circuit breaker history, notification settings, dashboard local/remote settings, secrets/auth prerequisites, environments.json/Firebase target, install snapshot/reconcile state, PM-tool credentials, MCP server readiness, and generated dashboard state. Expose the inventory through CLI JSON/text and dashboard Settings/Setup state with safe commands, human-required steps, and dashboard availability hints.
steps: Add a config inventory model with fields: id, title, scope (machine/project/plan/capability/secret/runtime), status, editable, safe_command, dashboard_mutation_shape, human_required, current_value_summary, owner_file_or_env, risks, and related doctor probes.

Create inventory providers for global config, project config, projects registry, agent manifest, roles, runtime_evidence, human_gates/protected_paths/plans_dir/default_target_env, quota caps/calibration/state, circuit breaker state/history, notifications, dashboard config, capabilities/adapters, MCP, environments/Firebase target, secrets/auth, install snapshot/reconcile, and PM-tool credentials.
Expose `dontpanic config inventory [--project NAME|PATH] [--format text|json]` or an equivalent setup-oriented command.
Render the same inventory into dashboard Settings/Setup state so the UI can show editable cards and human-required setup cards.

For safe edits, emit exact commands that route through existing validated surfaces (`roles set`, `project config set`, `capabilities setup`, `quota-caps init`, `calibrate-claude`, `reconcile`, `projects add --onboard`).
For secrets/auth/provider setup, never print or write secrets; show human-required steps and verification commands only.

When one or more inventory items require human input, include one response-level dashboard_hint with active_url when a local dashboard is running or start_command when it is not; item-level records may include a dashboard_hint_ref but must not duplicate the full text.
For optional capabilities, explain readiness and why they are optional so core DontPanic use is not blocked by Firebase/Discord/Linear/GCP setup.
Add a setup/update planner that can generate a DontPanic plan or ActionChoice list for incomplete setup areas instead of forcing the interactive agent to invent next steps.
Add tests for inventory completeness, JSON shape, dashboard state shape, safe-command validation, secret redaction/no-secret-output, optional-vs-required classification, and project-scoped overrides.
features.acceptance: (1) A human or interactive agent can run one command (`dontpanic config inventory [--project NAME|PATH] [--format text|json]`) to see all relevant DontPanic configuration surfaces and their status. (2) Inventory covers global config, project config, registry, manifest, roles, runtime evidence, gates/protected paths, quota/caps/calibration, circuit breakers, notifications, dashboard, capabilities/adapters, MCP, environments/Firebase, secrets/auth, install snapshot/reconcile, PM-tool credentials, and generated state. (2b) Status is correct, not optimistic: e.g. a roles provider whose resolved implementer/auditor is not in AGENT_REGISTRY reports a non-ok status (invalid/unrunnable), never `ok`. (2c) The non-optimistic-status rule is a GENERAL invariant across EVERY provider, not a per-example fix: any provider whose underlying state is invalid, incomplete, or unrunnable reports a non-ok status — e.g. roles not in AGENT_REGISTRY, quota caps present but calibration absent, capabilities/adapters known-but-unconfigured, manifest present-but-unloadable, etc. A single parametrized test asserts, for EACH provider, that an invalid/incomplete underlying state yields a non-ok status (so the suite proves the invariant holds class-wide, not just for the roles example). (4) Optional integrations are labeled optional and do not block core use. (5) Safe edits route through existing commands; secrets/auth steps are human-required and never echo secret values. (5b) "Safe command" means VALIDATED: every non-null `safe_command` PASSES `command_validation.validate_command_tokens` (stripping the `dontpanic`/`python -m dontpanic_orchestrate` prefix); a build/start/serve command (e.g. `dashboard build`, `mcp serve`) is NOT an edit affordance and must not be emitted as an inventory item's safe_command. (7) The setup/update planner can emit ActionChoices or a draft DontPanic plan for incomplete setup/update work. (8) Tests cover at least ten inventory providers, secret-safe output, the non-ok-on-invalid-roles case, AND a round-trip asserting EVERY non-null safe_command passes validate_command_tokens. (Scope, per D037 split: F008 is the inventory model + providers + CLI + validated safe_commands + correct status. Dashboard Settings/Setup rendering, active/inactive dashboard-hint auto-detection, and edit-vs-action affordance distinction are delegated to F013 and are OUT OF SCOPE for F008.) (2d) Tight-scope close-out requirements: the patch touches NO dashboard/* or dashboard settings files (that is F013 scope) — a patch modifying dashboard/* fails this AC; the present-but-UNLOADABLE config provider reports non-ok; a TRIPPED circuit-breaker provider reports non-ok; and the parametrized invariant test uses REAL invalid-state inputs (an actually-unloadable config file and an actually-tripped breaker) that fail before the fix and pass after — not trivially-passing weak cases. (2e) The non-optimistic-status invariant is implemented as a SINGLE shared status-derivation helper applied uniformly by EVERY provider (not per-provider ad-hoc checks); a `--project NAME|PATH` selector that does not resolve reports a non-ok/error status and never silently falls back to machine-only inventory; and ONE exhaustive parametrized test asserts, for EVERY provider, that a representative invalid/incomplete/unrunnable underlying state yields a non-ok status — covering at minimum unloadable config files, a tripped breaker, quota caps-present-but-calibration-absent, quota-state missing/unreadable, global_config/roles defaults that are not runnable executors, unsupported roles, an invalid manifest, and stale onboarding — with the test failing before the shared helper is applied and passing after. Per-provider patches that satisfy only the listed examples do NOT meet this AC.

features.description: Dashboard Settings/Setup rendering for the F008 config inventory. F008 builds the inventory model + CLI + validated safe_commands, but the inventory is not rendered into the dashboard UI, dashboard hints are not auto-detected (only emitted when a caller passes dashboard_url), and build/start commands are shown as edit affordances. This slice renders the inventory as dashboard Settings/Setup cards, auto-detects the active dashboard singleton for the response-level hint, and distinguishes edit affordances (safe_command) from run-actions (build/start).
steps: Wire collect_inventory() output into the dashboard build so Settings/Setup cards render from the same inventory the CLI shows.

Auto-detect a running dashboard singleton to populate the response-level dashboard_hint active_url; fall back to the start command when none is running (no manual dashboard_url pass-through required).
Render edit affordances (validated safe_command) distinctly from run-actions (e.g. dashboard build/start, mcp serve), which must not appear as edit commands on a card.
Add tests: dashboard cards render for >=10 providers; active vs inactive hint auto-detection; dashboard-hint dedup; no build/start command rendered as an edit affordance.

(2) The response-level dashboard_hint auto-detects a running dashboard singleton for active_url and falls back to the start command when none runs — without the caller manually passing dashboard_url. (5) Tests prove cards render for >=10 providers, active/inactive hint auto-detection, dashboard-hint dedup, and that no build/start command is emitted as an edit affordance.

features.description: Active-run plan drift reconciliation. Detect and reconcile plan changes made while DontPanic is running, especially when one interactive agent edits the plan while another interactive agent or worker volley is operating from older context. Capture a plan fingerprint at dispatch/start, watch or re-check plan artifacts before paid calls, before auditor calls, before gate finalization, and before signoff. Classify drift as safe additive (e.g. new decision note), requires refresh (e.g. changed acceptance, feature list, dependencies, gates, roles, max_iterations), or blocking (e.g. allowed_paths/forbidden_decisions scope change). Emit a concise ActionChoice and dashboard item that tells the operator whether DontPanic refreshed context automatically, needs redispatch, or needs human reconciliation.
steps: Define a plan-run fingerprint over plan.md frontmatter, features.json, decisions.jsonl, objective_contract.json, gate-state, and any files that affect dispatch semantics.
Record the fingerprint and source file mtimes/content hashes at dispatch start and in active supervisor state.
Before each expensive/policy-relevant step (implementer call, auditor call, signoff/finalization), recompute the fingerprint and compare.
Classify drift: additive ledger-only, context-refresh-required, or blocking-policy-change.
For additive ledger-only drift, update active state and continue while recording the reconciliation event.
For context-refresh-required drift, pause before the next paid call and offer exact redispatch/resume guidance with refreshed plan context.
For blocking policy/scope drift, require human acknowledgement before continuing.
Add dashboard/CLI ActionChoice output that names changed files, impact, recommended action, and whether budget was protected by pausing before the next call.
Add tests for concurrent edits to decisions.jsonl, features.json acceptance, loop_caps.max_iterations, human_gates, roles, allowed_paths, and objective_contract.
features.acceptance: (1) Dispatch records a plan-run fingerprint BEFORE the plan/features are loaded into memory and before any paid agent call, so every later drift check compares against true dispatch-start disk state (AC1 + codex #2: baseline must precede the plan load at supervisor.py:1371, not follow it). (2) Plan changes during a run are detected before the next paid agent call or signoff finalization, on the VOLLEY dispatch path. (3) Additive decisions.jsonl drift is reconciled in-place without stopping, with an event recorded (AC3). (4) Feature/acceptance/gate/role/loop-cap drift PAUSES the volley (paused_on_drift) and tells the operator how to refresh/redispatch (AC4). (5) Drift detection FAILS CLOSED (codex #3): a fingerprint/reconcile error pauses or raises rather than swallowing the exception and continuing on possibly-stale context — a safety mechanism must not fail open. (6) Tests simulate another process editing plan files mid-run on the volley path and prove DontPanic does not continue on stale context silently, incl. a fail-closed test that the drift check raising does NOT silently proceed. (Single-agent dispatch coverage, scope/policy human-ack workflow, and CLI/dashboard one-action surfacing are SPLIT to F014 — D056.)

features.description: Skill invocation rubrics — CORE engine (split from the original 14-AC F011 per D060). Add a validated `invocation:` SKILL.md frontmatter schema and a PURE skill-invocation evaluator that reads an injected SkillInvocationContext (applicable-skills output, skill frontmatter, plan metadata, goal_type, changed files, config-inventory summaries, budget state, lifecycle stage, available commands) and emits typed SkillAction records with the five recommendation values. Deterministic risk precedence and the never_suggest opt-out live here. The auditable auto-run ALLOWLIST artifact + doctor/F008 visibility (F015) and the CLI/dashboard surfaces + missing-input one-action + migration command (F016) are separate slices.
steps: Define the `invocation:` SKILL.md frontmatter schema (mode enum, lifecycle stages, required inputs, risk flags, evidence target, optional command template) with a validator that is a no-op for skills lacking the block.
Add a pure SkillInvocationEvaluator taking an injected SkillInvocationContext and emitting typed SkillAction records; no I/O, no network, no execution — recommendation only.
Implement and document deterministic risk-precedence rules in the evaluator, including the contradictory-metadata diagnostic SkillAction.
Default metadata-less skills to suggest/not_applicable; never auto_run.

Treat the auto-run allowlist as an INJECTED predicate (is_command_allowlisted) supplied by F015; the engine returns auto_run-eligible vs blocked based on that predicate's result, but does not own the allowlist artifact.
Add built-in rubric fixtures for the representative skills listed in AC13.
Tests: each recommendation class, no-auto fallback, never_suggest opt-out, risk precedence with contradictory metadata, and missing-input handling — all at the pure-evaluator level.
features.acceptance: (1) `SKILL.md` supports validated `invocation:` metadata (mode in {auto_readonly, auto_safe, suggest, approval_required, never_auto, never_suggest}, lifecycle stages, required inputs, risk flags, evidence target — REQUIRED for the auto-eligible modes (auto_readonly, auto_safe) and OPTIONAL for suggest/approval_required/never_auto/never_suggest, which never auto-execute and so have no evidence to target — optional command template) WITHOUT breaking skills that lack it. (2) A pure evaluator emits typed SkillAction records (skill_name, recommendation, reason, risk, missing_inputs, exact_command-when-safe, evidence_target, approval_required) from an injected pure SkillInvocationContext; recommendation values are auto_run, suggest, approval_required, blocked_missing_inputs, not_applicable. (3) Skills without invocation metadata default to suggest or not_applicable and are NEVER auto_run. (6) Risk precedence is deterministic and tested: explicit never_auto/never_suggest wins; external writes, paid actions, indefinite loops, credentialed production reads, network access, repo mutation, and missing inputs each downgrade/block auto_run regardless of declared mode; contradictory metadata yields a diagnostic SkillAction rather than silently trusting the unsafe declaration. (12) never_suggest (or equivalent opt-out) prevents noisy/toolkit skills from appearing in recommendations. (13) Representative current skills are covered by fixtures: autoresearch, security-review, eval-harness, test-runner, cost-model, changelog, browser-use, revenue-check, github-pr, worktree-isolation, subagent-driven-dev, prompt-optimizer, printing-press-adapter. (14a) Tests prove each recommendation class, the no-auto fallback for metadata-less skills, the never_suggest opt-out, risk precedence with contradictory metadata, and missing-input handling at the evaluator level. NOTE: the allowlist-gated auto_run path (AC4/AC5/AC7) is F015 and the CLI/dashboard/migration surfaces (AC8-11) are F016; this slice may classify a read-only skill as auto_run-eligible but treats the actual allowlist check as an injected predicate provided by F015.

features.description: Skill auto-run ALLOWLIST artifact + approval gating (split from F011 per D060). Make the auto-run allowlist a first-class, versioned, auditable artifact that the F011 evaluator consults via its injected predicate, and enforce that mutating/credentialed/networked/paid/external-write/indefinite-loop skills are never silently executed. doctor/reconcile and the F008 config inventory expose missing/stale/conflicting allowlist state.
steps: Define the auto-run allowlist as a versioned, auditable artifact recording skill name, command template or command prefix, allowed mode, owner/approval metadata, version/hash, and rationale.
Provide the allowlist-check predicate the F011 evaluator injects: a read-only skill becomes auto_run-eligible ONLY when all required inputs exist AND its exact command matches an allowlist entry.
Enforce that mutating, credentialed, networked, paid, external-write, or indefinite-loop skills resolve to approval_required or suggest and are never silently executed.
Surface missing/stale/conflicting allowlist state through doctor/reconcile and the F008 config inventory.
Tests: command-allowlist enforcement (allowed vs absent vs prefix-mismatch), approval-required skills never invoked, and doctor/reconcile/F008 allowlist-visibility output.
features.acceptance: (4) Read-only bounded skills auto-run (or become auto-runnable) ONLY when required inputs exist AND the exact command is present in a versioned, auditable auto-run allowlist. (5) The allowlist has owner/approval metadata, version/hash, rationale, and command template/prefix fields; doctor/reconcile AND the F008 config inventory expose missing/stale/conflicting allowlist state. (7) Mutating, credentialed, networked, paid, external-write, or indefinite-loop skills require approval or are suggested — never silently executed. (14b) Tests prove command-allowlist enforcement, doctor/reconcile allowlist visibility, and that approval-required skills are never invoked by the recommender.

features.description: Skill recommendation SURFACES + migration (split from F011 per D060). Expose the F011/F015 SkillAction set through `dontpanic skills recommend` and the dashboard with identical data, route missing required inputs through F007's ActionChoice/dashboard-hint dedup as ONE concise action, use F008 config inventory to explain unavailable credentials/binaries/capabilities, and add a migration path that proposes starting rubrics for high-value skills lacking invocation metadata without blocking core use.
steps: Add `dontpanic skills recommend --plan <plan> [--stage STAGE] [--format text|json]` (or equivalent) and include the same SkillAction recommendations in dashboard action/setup state.
Render identical SkillAction data on CLI and dashboard: skill, recommendation, reason, risk, command, approval requirement, and evidence target.
Route missing required inputs through the F007 ActionChoice/dashboard-hint system as ONE concise question/action naming only the missing blocker (no long prompting loop).
Integrate with the F008 config inventory so unavailable credentials/binaries/capabilities/absent eval commands explain why a skill is blocked instead of being silently skipped.

Add a migration path: `dontpanic skills rubric --suggest <skill>` (or equivalent) proposes starting invocation metadata from current frontmatter/triggers/tool requirements/risk heuristics; doctor flags high-value skills without rubrics without blocking core use.
Tests: dashboard JSON shape parity with CLI, missing-input single-action behavior, F008-explained blockers, and migration-suggestion output.
features.acceptance: (8) Missing inputs produce ONE concise ActionChoice or dashboard action naming only the missing blocker. (9) CLI and dashboard render the SAME SkillAction data (reason, risk, command, approval requirement, evidence target). (10) The recommender uses the F008 config inventory to explain unavailable credentials/binaries/capabilities and F007 dashboard-hint deduplication for human decisions. (11) Existing skills have a migration path: a rubric suggestion command or doctor advisory identifies high-value skills missing invocation metadata and proposes safe starting rubrics WITHOUT blocking core use. (14c) Tests prove dashboard JSON shape, missing-input handling at the surface, F008-explained blockers, and migration suggestion output.

features.description: Dashboard singleton guard, availability discovery, and final docs. Prevent multiple local dashboard servers from accumulating by adding a singleton registry or pidfile with stale-process pruning and `--replace` behavior. Expose a lightweight dashboard status helper so CLI/agent guidance can tell users whether the dashboard is running and what URL to open. Update README, getting started, and changelog to document the new agent/repo onboarding flow, skill invocation recommendations, and the operator-vs-worker distinction.
steps: Add a dashboard serve singleton record under the canonical DontPanic home, or reuse active_supervisors with a distinct dashboard kind if that is cleaner.
On `dontpanic dashboard serve`, detect an existing live dashboard process for the same home and refuse with the existing URL plus remediation.
Add `--replace` or `--force-single` to stop or supersede the existing singleton when requested.
Prune stale singleton records when the recorded pid is gone.
Add a dashboard status helper returning active URL/project/scope when running, or the exact serve command when not running, plus a response-level render helper that dedupes dashboard hints.
Route operations guidance and config inventory through the status helper rather than reimplementing dashboard discovery.
Keep port-bind OSError handling for normal same-port conflicts.
Add tests for first serve, second serve refusal, stale record prune, replace behavior, and once-mode cleanup.

Update README.md and docs/GETTING_STARTED.md with the new `agent brief`, `projects add --onboard`, role assignment, configuration inventory/setup cockpit, skill invocation recommendations, `doctor --agent`, `doctor --project`, `what-now`/operations guidance, and `orchestrate` flow.
Add CHANGELOG.md entry for the product-facing onboarding and dashboard serve behavior.
features.acceptance: (1) Starting a second dashboard serve in the same DontPanic home refuses with an actionable message. (2) Stale singleton records are pruned. (3) `--replace` or equivalent intentionally replaces a live singleton. (4) Dashboard status helper returns active URL when running and start command when inactive. (5) Shared render helper emits the dashboard hint once per response even when many items require human input. (6) Existing bind failure handling still works. (7) Tests cover singleton behavior, status helper, and deduped hint rendering without opening a browser. (8) README and getting-started docs show the complete new-agent, new-repo, role-assignment, config-inventory/setup, budget/iteration guidance, skill invocation recommendation, and dashboard decision flow. (9) CHANGELOG documents the operator-visible changes. (10) Full targeted test suite passes.

features.description: Plan-drift reconciliation — coverage + enforcement surfaces split from F009 (D056). Guards the single-agent dispatch path with the same drift reconciliation as the volley path, enforces a real human-acknowledgement workflow for blocking scope/policy drift, and surfaces ONE concise reconciliation action in CLI + dashboard.
features.acceptance: (1) The single-agent dispatch path (cli.py dispatch_single_agent) is guarded by the SAME F009 drift reconciliation as the volley path — no paid single-agent call proceeds on stale plan context (codex F009 #4). (2) Blocking scope/policy drift (allowed_paths / forbidden_decisions, AC5) is enforced as a real human-acknowledgement workflow: the run pauses and requires an explicit operator ack (e.g. `dontpanic approve <plan> drift:<class>` or equivalent) before any further paid call — not merely labeled human_required in plan_drift.py (codex F009 #5). (3) CLI and dashboard show ONE concise reconciliation action, not repeated warnings (F009 AC6). (4) Tests cover: single-agent path pauses on blocking drift; the scope/policy ack workflow blocks-then-resumes; and the CLI/dashboard emit exactly one reconciliation action.
steps: Guard cli.dispatch_single_agent with the same plan_drift baseline (early, fail-closed) + check_and_reconcile as dispatch_volley; no single-agent paid call proceeds on stale plan context.

Enforce a human-ack workflow for blocking scope/policy drift (allowed_paths / forbidden_decisions): pause + require an explicit operator approval before any further paid call, not merely a human_required label.
Surface exactly ONE reconciliation action in CLI and dashboard (no repeated warnings).
Tests: single-agent path pauses on blocking drift; scope/policy ack blocks-then-resumes; CLI/dashboard emit one reconciliation action.
